chunks.text: Today we will talk about Antigua and Barbuda.
It is a small island country in the Caribbean Sea.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Antigua and Barbuda?
Antigua and Barbuda is in the Caribbean.
It is east of Puerto Rico and north of Guadalupe.
It is made of two main islands, Antigua and Barbuda.
There are also some small islands.
What is the capital city?
The capital city is St.
John's.
It is on the island of Antigua.
St.
John's has colorful buildings, markets and a busy harbor.
Barbuda is smaller and has few people, but many birds and beautiful beaches.
How many people live there?
About 100,000 people live in Antigua and Barbuda.
Most people live on Antigua.
The country is peaceful and friendly.
What language do people speak?
The official language is English.
Many people speak Caribbean English with a local accent.
It is easy to understand and full of warm expressions.
What is the weather like?
The weather is warm and sunny all year.
It is usually around 25 to 30 degrees Celsius.
There are two seasons, the dry season from December to April.
The rainy season from May to November.
There can be hurricanes between August and October.
What does it look like?
The country has white sand beaches, blue sea and coral reefs, green hills and palm trees, lagoons and clear skies.
Antigua has 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
What animals live there?
You can see frigate birds with red chests, especially on Barbuda pelicans, herons and other birds.
Fish, sea turtles and dolphins, goats, donkeys and chickens on farms.
The Codrington Lagoon is a special bird sanctuary.
What do people eat?
The food is fresh, tropical and flavorful.
People eat fish, lobster and conch, rice, plantains and sweet potatoes, fruits like mangoes, pineapples and bananas.
Popular dishes, fungi and pepper pot, cornmeal with vegetable stew, national dish, salt fish and chop up, dried fish with mashed vegetables.
Johnny cakes, fried bread, goat water, a spicy goat meat soup.
What do people drink?
People drink water and fresh juice, coconut water, sorrel, a red drink made from flowers, mobby made from tree bark, adults may drink rum punch or local beer.
Cold drinks are popular because of the warm weather.
What is life like?
Life is relaxed and social.
People enjoy talking with friends and neighbors, swimming and boating, dancing and music, spending time with family.
People are friendly and say hello with a smile.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, November 1st carnival in July and August with costumes and dancing, Christmas and New Year's with food and fireworks, Labor Day, Emancipation Day and other national events.
Carnival is the biggest celebration full of color and joy.
Some fun facts about Antigua and Barbuda.
The country became independent in 1981.
The flag is red, black, blue, yellow and white with a sun.
The frigate bird is the national bird.
The islands were once a British colony.
Antigua and Barbuda is famous for cricket.
Now you know many things about Antigua and Barbuda.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the beaches, weather, culture and animals.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
